title: Slide 14
notes: I considered how minor changes in mechanics can drastically change chess Here are some examples of the starting board eﬀecting gameplay

title: Slide 15
notes: by simply changing the starting position of pieces, the necessity to remember opening lines in prevented instead, players are forced to rely on opening theory and intuition this helps prevent repetitiveness in the early stages of the game similarly…

title: Slide 16
notes: …facing an army of pawns changes all gameplay dynamics entirely. sacriﬁcing pieces becomes far more common and the board feels more claustrophobic. the opposite of claustrophobia in chess is…

title: Slide 17
notes: …borderless chess the limitless board increases the value of pieces with range less linear & diagonal movement. the lack of constriction also opens the board more easily for the rooks, changing the early-game theory.

title: Slide 18
notes: I then looked into diﬀerent chess pieces and their movements You can imagine how replacing a conventional chess piece with one of the following would distance the game from traditional chess

title: Slide 19
notes: here is an example of a new piece, a Ferz, that can only move one square diagonally or can jump two squares diagonally quite unlike any other chess piece

title: Slide 20
notes: in a similar realm, this piece: called a Wazir, can only move one square horizontally or vertically it can also also jump

title: Slide 21
notes: new pieces do not have to have completely new pieces either, they can be a play on existing movement mechanics or could blend two or more pieces movement mechanics into one

title: Slide 22
notes: the nightrider piece is an interesting example of how a minor change to an existing movement mechanic can have big changes the piece is particularly interesting as it builds on the knight’s hopping movement mechanic but does not restrict it. this is an interesting start point when thinking about the movement of toads in relation to chess pieces.

title: Slide 23
notes: the Empress is a hybrid between a rook and a knight combining an irregular and diﬃcult to visualise movement system with a rigid and predictable one

title: Slide 24
notes: to summarise, changing, adding and removing pieces drastically changes gameplay theory. the inclusion of further variables forces players to think about how to use the new pieces and will have to conclude their value independently. instead of relying on pre-calculated strategies the game becomes more intuitive which, in my opinion, adds a further degree of playfulness to an otherwise rigid game.
